newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI CAUTIOUSLY HIGHER, WINDOW-DRESSING SEEN.
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI CAUTIOUSLY HIGHER, WINDOW-DRESSING SEEN.

text.p: * Shares end marginally higher, bolstered by a late spurt
in Nokia. Hartwall hits new life high. Rautaruukki perky on
steel prices prospects. End-of-month window-dressing seen.
* Volume sturdy 317.06 mln markka, 36 pct in Nokia
* HEX +0.14 pct at 2,174.14, adv-decl 47-33, 24 unch
Shares closed a fairly active
session moderately higher on Monday, paring earlier losses on
the back of a late rally in Nokia, brokers said.
Nokia ended official trade 1.50 markka higher at 203.90,
although it opened slightly lower on Wall Street. Turnover was
fairly active for Nokia at 132 million markka.
Brokers spotted some end-of-month window-dressing,
particularly in trading in smaller company shares.
Forestries remained subdued as worries mounted that planned
pulp price hikes would not go through, brokers said.
"It seems highly unlikely now that producers can go ahead
with the planned pulp price increases," one broker said.
Insurers remained well-bid on continuing talk of near-term
restructuring of ownership in the sector.
Speculation has spread in the market that banking group
Merita, which has major holdings in Pohjola and Sampo, might
dispose of or reduce its stake in the insurance companies.
Beverages group Hartwall closed at a new life high 150.00
markka, up seven, buoyed by its stronger-than-expected
January-August results released last week.
-- Veera Heinonen, Helsinki newsroom + 358-0-680 50 240
